welcome.label: Welcome · the still canal

parts.label: 📰 The front page
parts.title: Pelican Canal goes still and green

parts.label: 🌬️ Today
parts.title: Can moving air and water do work?
parts.body: Wind energy, water energy, and what makes a wheel spin faster.

welcome.script:
(Blow on your hand.) Feel that? That’s moving air. Can something you can’t even see do real work?

[ON SCREEN: The front page]
Pelican Canal is back in the news. The water has gone still and green, and readers sent in ideas to get it moving.

[ON SCREEN: Today]
Today you help Sam judge which idea really works. Read the front page and the three entries just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · the mystery tower (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Peek through your fingers.) When I only see a little, I have to think like a detective.

[ON SCREEN: The mystery tower]
This tower stands in a field with no wires at all. What could it be for?

[ON SCREEN: Fewer tiles, more stars]
Lift one tile at a time and guess. Press Listen on Sam’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

part1.label: Part 1 · the drop race (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Hold up a flat sheet of paper and a crumpled one.) Same paper. Which lands first?

[ON SCREEN: The drop race]
Predict, then let go. If air is really nothing, they should tie. Press Listen.

part2.label: Part 2 · turn the valve (Clue 3)
part2.script:
(Turn on a faucet a little, then all the way.) Trickle… whoosh!

[ON SCREEN: Turn the valve]
Drag the red valve handle and watch the waterwheel, the stone and the lamp. Then close it all the way and press “Spin by itself.” Can a wheel make its own energy? Find out.

explore.label: Part 3 · count the red blade (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Hold up a pinwheel, or one finger spinning in a circle.) One, two, three…

[ON SCREEN: Count the red blade]
Scientists count carefully. Run Test 1. Then change just ONE thing, the wind or the way it faces, and tap every time the red blade passes the top. If you have a pinwheel, try it for real, too! Press Listen.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Four clues: pick the Bright Idea that really works.

[ON SCREEN: Florida’s zero]
Then guess how many wind farms Florida has. The answer might surprise you!

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Last, two short answers, your wind and water model with a labeled sketch, and your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Wind isn’t real energy. It’s just air moving. It doesn’t do anything.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
Doesn’t do anything? Hmm. Think about that flat paper, and the fan.

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts, then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.script:
(Blow on your hand again.) Now you know: that little breeze is real energy.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and the Bright Idea ribbon goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Bonus]
Want more wind? Try sailing the canal.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
